tasks.title: InterAgentCommunication: add optional abort_reason struct field
tasks.description: Add optional `abort_reason: Schema.optional(Schema.Struct({ reason: Schema.String, details: Schema.String }))` field to the InterAgentCommunication Schema.Class in packages/opencode/src/agent/inter-agent-communication.ts. The field MUST be optional (additive change, no schema migration). Place it AFTER `correlation_id` and BEFORE the closing `)`. Add a multi-line comment above the field explaining it carries the structured ABORT reason payload when a subagent emits `ABORT(<reason>): <details>` as its last assistant line (D11 Wave 4 ABORT protocol). After the change: (a) `bun typecheck` from packages/opencode passes; (b) all existing inter-agent-communication.test.ts tests still pass — the additive optional field MUST NOT break pre-existing constructors that omit abort_reason. Extend inter-agent-communication.test.ts with: (1) a constructor test that creates an InterAgentCommunication with abort_reason supplied and asserts both fields are preserved, (2) a schema-decode test that decodes a payload with abort_reason and validates both fields, (3) a JSON roundtrip test for abort_reason. Do NOT modify control.ts or mailbox.ts — sendInterAgentCommunication already passes the whole InterAgentCommunication object through Mailbox.send unchanged, so the optional field travels through. The runtime parsing of ABORT and the population of this field land in T2. Commit message: `wave 4 T1: add abort_reason to InterAgentCommunication schema (additive)`.

tasks.title: control.ts: completion-watcher parses ABORT set-phrase + populates structured abort_reason
tasks.description:
In control.ts add a top-level helper `parseAbortReason(body: string): { reason: string; details: string } | undefined` colocated with `extractText` / `looksLikeMissingDeliverable` (near L173-207). Spec: trim trailing whitespace; take the LAST non-empty line; if it matches `^ABORT\(([a-z_]+)\):\s*(.+?)\s*$` (strict line-anchor regex per GOTCHA `word-boundary-regex-vs-prose-collisions` and WAVE.md Gotcha #1), return `{ reason: m[1], details: m[2] }`; otherwise return undefined. The match runs on the EXTRACTED body (the same body the safety-net heuristic and the notification builder see) so the parser sees the joined text-parts only, never tool-call payloads.

In the completion-watcher (control.ts:816-920), AFTER `body` is computed but BEFORE / alongside the InterAgentCommunication construction, call `const abortParsed = parseAbortReason(body)`. Pass `abort_reason: abortParsed` to the `new InterAgentCommunication({ ... })` block (optional field — undefined when no ABORT match). The human-readable notification body is unchanged — the ABORT line stays inside `content` so legacy consumers (TUI, log scrapers) see the literal `ABORT(...): ...` text; the new structured field is the parsed payload for supervisors that want to dispatch on it.

Do NOT couple ABORT recognition to safety-net warning logic; the two pass over the body independently. An ABORT body that is short + single-line + contains a status word may also trip `looksLikeMissingDeliverable` — that is acceptable; the warning is informational, the structured payload is the actionable signal.

Extend control.test.ts with a new describe block `AgentControl D11 ABORT recognition` containing tests: (1) child emits `ABORT(spec_wrong): bad spec.` as its last assistant text → parent's notification has `abort_reason: { reason: 'spec_wrong', details: 'bad spec.' }`; (2) child emits a multi-line message ending in `ABORT(approach_failed): tried 3x.` → abort_reason parsed correctly from the LAST line; (3) child emits a normal completion with no ABORT line → `abort_reason` is undefined on the notification; (4) child emits `ABORT(custom_reason): foo` (an unrecognized reason — not in the official six) → abort_reason still forwarded with `reason: 'custom_reason'` (graceful degradation per WAVE.md Gotcha #2 — the runtime does not enforce the enum, only the prose does). Each test follows the existing D5 pattern (`registerRunLoop` writes an assistant message via `writeAssistantMessage`, spawn child, sleep, drain root's mailbox, find notification by author).

Also append a GOTCHAS.md entry under `### agentcontrol-d11-abort-line-parser-last-line-only` documenting: regex anchors to the LAST non-empty line (not anywhere in body), so an ABORT mention inside a paragraph or code block doesn't trip the parser; unrecognized reasons are forwarded but only the six official reasons are documented.

Verify: `bun typecheck`; `bun test src/agent/control.test.ts` all pass (existing 100% line coverage preserved on control.ts — the new parser + watcher branch are reachable via the four new tests). Commit message: `wave 4 T2: parse ABORT set-phrase in completion-watcher + structured abort_reason payload`.

tasks.title: Prose: ABORT section in multi-agent-subagent.txt + brief refs in 3 base prompts + ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md note
tasks.description:
FOUR deliverables: (A) Append a new `## ABORT — structured failure exits` section to multi-agent-subagent.txt AFTER the existing `## Delivery contract` section (end of file). The section MUST: (1) state ABORT is for structured failure exits when the spawner needs to know WHY not just THAT you failed, (2) enumerate the SIX official reasons in a bulleted list with one-line definitions: `spec_wrong`, `transient_tool_error`, `out_of_scope`, `context_full`, `approach_failed`, `user_question`, (3) declare the format `ABORT(<reason>): <one-line details>` and that it MUST be the LAST line of your last assistant message, (4) note that the runtime parses it and surfaces a structured payload to the spawner, (5) clarify that ABORT does NOT auto-close — still call send_message to deliver partial work and close_agent in the following turn, (6) note that unrecognized reasons are forwarded but the six standard reasons are what supervisors recognize.

(B) Brief ABORT reference added to each of: `general/anthropic.txt` (§Response format, after the existing failure-reporting bullet), `general/gemini.txt` (§Response Format, after existing failure-reporting bullet), `explore.txt` (§Response Format, after existing bullet 4 'Explicit negatives'). Each reference MUST be one short line (1-3 sentences max) pointing to the ABORT section in the multi-agent coordination guidance and naming `ABORT(<reason>): <details>` literally. Example wording (adapt per file's voice): `For structured failure exits, end your last assistant message with `ABORT(<reason>): <details>` so your spawner can supervise — see the ABORT section in your multi-agent coordination guidance.`

(C) Update ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md: add a one-line cross-reference note next to the existing `ABORT REASONS YOU MAY USE:` section (near L115-124 in the planner / generator / evaluator spawn message template) saying: `Note: as of Wave 4, these reasons are PARSED by the runtime — control.ts surfaces a structured abort_reason payload on the spawner's mailbox notification when a subagent emits this set-phrase as its last assistant line.`

(D) NO PROMPT_SURFACES.md edits needed unless you discover the file's content map omits the ABORT ownership (it currently lists D11 under multi-agent-subagent.txt at line 70 — already correct).

Constraints: (a) Do NOT introduce any of the FORBIDDEN_PHRASES from test/prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts (the test asserts these stay absent post-Wave-1). (b) The REQUIRED_PHRASE `See the delivery contract in your multi-agent coordination guidance.` MUST remain present in each of the 3 base prompts (already there from Wave 1). (c) Preserve all caveman output rules / response-format sections verbatim except for the targeted bullet addition. (d) Preserve the existing structure of multi-agent-subagent.txt (Delivery contract stays as-is; ABORT is a NEW SECTION after it).

Verify: `bun test test/prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts` passes — existing 27 tests stay green. T4 will add Wave 4 prose grep tests; this task does NOT add them — T4 owns the test suite extension. Commit message: `wave 4 T3: ABORT protocol prose in subagent prompts + ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md note`.

tasks.title: Tests: INV-D-12..14 integration invariants + Wave 4 prose grep tests
tasks.description:
Append THREE new `it.instance` tests to multi-agent-invariants.test.ts inside the existing `INTEGRATION_INVARIANTS — multi-agent surfaces` describe block, AFTER the INV-D-11 block (currently ending around L1687):

(1) `INV-D-12-abort-reason-delivered-as-structured-payload` — Child runLoop emits assistant message with text body ending in `ABORT(spec_wrong): details here.` Spawn child, sleep 80ms for completion watcher, drain root's mailbox, find the notification from the child path, assert: `note.abort_reason?.reason === 'spec_wrong'`, `note.abort_reason?.details === 'details here.'`. Also assert the human-readable `note.content` still contains the literal substring `ABORT(spec_wrong)` (so legacy consumers see it). Pattern: model the runLoop after INV-D-01 (write user + assistant message via sessions.updateMessage + updatePart, finish: 'tool-calls' is fine, return 'done').

(2) `INV-D-13-orchestrator-pivots-on-abort-approach-failed` — STUB ORCHESTRATOR pattern, NO real git. Tracks state in a local mutable structure. Spawn child whose runLoop emits `ABORT(approach_failed): tried 3 attempts, recommend reset.` as last assistant line. Assert: parent's notification carries `abort_reason: { reason: 'approach_failed', details: 'tried 3 attempts, recommend reset.' }`. Then the test acts as the stub orchestrator: reads abort_reason, decides 'pivot' (record in a local audit array), respawns a new child with refined initial_message (`initial_message: 'retry with context: ' + abort_reason.details` or similar). The respawn's runLoop emits a normal completion (no ABORT). Assert the second notification has NO abort_reason. Assert the audit array contains `['pivot:approach_failed']`. The test pins (a) runtime recognition of ABORT(approach_failed), (b) the runtime supports the pivot pattern (parent can read the structured payload + respawn).

(3) `INV-D-14-set-phrase-ladder-extended-to-all-subagent-types` — Two sub-cases: spawn a child with `agent_type: 'general'` AND a child with `agent_type: 'explore'`. Each child's runLoop emits an assistant message ending in `ABORT(out_of_scope): test`. Drain root's mailbox; find each notification by author path; assert each has `abort_reason: { reason: 'out_of_scope', details: 'test' }`. Validates runtime parses ABORT regardless of agent_type.

New prose grep tests in test/prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts under a new describe block `Wave 4 — ABORT protocol prose`:
  - multi-agent-subagent.txt contains `## ABORT` section header
  - multi-agent-subagent.txt contains literal `ABORT(<reason>): <details>` format string (or `ABORT(<reason>):`)
  - multi-agent-subagent.txt contains each of the SIX reason tags: `spec_wrong`, `transient_tool_error`, `out_of_scope`, `context_full`, `approach_failed`, `user_question`
  - For each of the 3 base prompts (anthropic, gemini, explore): file contains `ABORT(` substring (the brief reference)

Constraints: (a) NO mocks of AgentControl / Session / Mailbox — use the real services via testEffect (per WAVE.md Hard Rules and the existing pattern). (b) Each test must run RED against pre-T2 code (where abort_reason is always undefined on notifications) and GREEN against post-T2 code. (c) Tests must be self-contained — no shared state across tests, use local mutable arrays inside the test closure for the stub orchestrator. (d) For INV-D-13, the respawn uses the same task_name suffixed with `_v2` (e.g. `pivot/pivot_v2`) to avoid path collision.

Verify: `bun typecheck`; `bun test ./test/integration/multi-agent-invariants.test.ts` passes (>= 31 tests: 28 existing + 3 new); each new INV-D-* passes when filtered by exact slug; `bun test test/prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts` passes (>= 30 tests: 27 existing + new Wave 4 block); orchestrator artefacts (PLAN.json, CONTRACT.json) present at waves/wave_4/. Commit message: `wave 4 T4: INV-D-12..14 integration invariants + Wave 4 prose grep tests`.
